body:
`claimed:` taking this - starting with the app generate paths (the first table: `drill_reach`, `circle_fit`, `contour_open`, `cross_stock`, and the bare unitless numbers in `material`/`area`). Those sentences quote numbers the user typed, they are built in the app with the document's world in scope, and `app::units::of(world)` over the `geometry::units` formatters is already the lens every field on screen rides - so the refusal sentences can switch to `len`-style formatting at build time without touching any pure-crate signature. In mm documents the text stays byte-identical (the `len` law), inch documents get the divided numbers and the in suffix.

Pinning red on main first, following `blind_floor::the_gouge_clause_speaks_the_document_s_units`: same refusal, inch world, assert the numbers divide by 25.4 and the sentence says in, never mm; plus untouched-mm pins proving the mm sentences did not move.

Leaving the pure-crate `Display` refusals (`tools`/`motion`) as a follow-up PR: they need the structured-refusal-vs-`Unit`-argument call made first, and the constant-quoting ones (`spun`, `holder_profile`, `lathe_holder` limits) are machine numbers this issue explicitly excludes.
